name: Kashmiri

ancestors.notes: Indo-Aryan — Kashmiri is conventionally grouped here as the Dardic subgroup (Glottolog; Wali & Koul 1997), though its Indo-Iranian position is debated in the literature.

notes: Kashmiri (کٲشُر, कॉशुर), a Dardic (Northwestern Indo-Aryan) language, ~7 million speakers, official/scheduled language of Jammu & Kashmir (India) and taught/published in Pakistan-administered Azad Kashmir; the Eighth Schedule (Indian Constitution) scheduled language. Written in BOTH Perso-Arabic (the majority script, standardised by the J&K Academy of Art, Culture & Languages) and Devanagari (used mainly by Kashmiri Pandits); this spec covers PERSO-ARABIC. GRAPHEME KEYS: the consonant inventory is the familiar Urdu/Persian Perso-Arabic set plus the SAME three retroflex letters Urdu/Balochi/Sindhi add (ٹ ڈ ڑ), plus ؠ (U+0620, 'Kashmiri yeh', a letter this script alone uses). Kashmiri is UNUSUAL among Perso-Arabic-script languages for marking almost every vowel quality explicitly rather than leaving short vowels undotted: beyond the three shared Arabic vowel signs (fatha َ /a/, kasra ِ /i/, damma ُ /u/) it adds five KASHMIRI-SPECIFIC diacritics for vowels the Persian/Urdu inventory has no letter for at all -- hamza-above ٔ /ə/, hamza-below ٕ /ɨ/ (a central vowel with no Urdu/Persian equivalent), the long-alif variant ٲ /əː/, the ring-waw ۄ /ɔ/ and the wavy-hamza-below ٟ /ɨː/ (Wali & Koul 1997; Wikipedia 'Kashmiri alphabet'). Aspirated stops (تھ ٹھ پھ کھ چھ) earn their multigraph keys the same way Urdu's do: one phonological segment, not a cluster (AGENTS.md test 2). KNOWN GAP, documented rather than silently resolved: Kashmiri Unicode text in the wild is NOT diacritic-encoding-standardised -- fonts/keyboards disagree on codepoints for the same phonetic vowel, and this spec's mapping for ۆ (U+06C6, tentatively /oː/), ٗ (U+0657, tentatively /uː/), ٚ (U+065A) and ٛ (U+065B, both tentatively variants of /ɨ(ː)/) is a best-effort reading of the WikiPron gold's actual character distribution (`kas_arab_broad.tsv`), not yet cross-checked letter-by-letter against a dedicated Kashmiri-orthography monograph; a future pass should replace the tentative four with a cited disambiguation. STRESS: Wali & Koul (1997) describe Kashmiri stress as predictable from syllable weight and not distinguishing lexical items; left unencoded here, a documented exemption rather than an omission. SMOKE CHECKS against `kas_arab_broad.tsv` (WikiPron, Wiktionary-scraped): آب /aːb/ 'water'-like item -> gold 'aː b' (spec: آ=aː, ب=b, matches); آزاد -> gold 'aː z aː d' (آ=aː, ز=z, ا=aː, د=d, matches); آسُن -> gold 'aː s u n' (آ=aː, س=s, ُ=u, ن=n, matches). TIER: `research` -- sourced (Wali & Koul 1997; PHOIBLE-class attested inventory), stress exemption documented, and `kas_arab_broad.tsv` (751 rows, WikiPron/Wiktionary scrape, `crowd-scraped` provenance, registered below) is scored in `scripts/benchmark.py` with a PER recorded in `benchmarks/results.json`.
